title: VF-018: the heap proof tier under JBMC and auto --confirm, with the second attempt on Z3 for products JBMC's SAT solver can't relate
description: The nine ignored tests of lib/tests/heap.rs, unchanged, at JBMC's default limit of 600 s. Four of them have failed since 2026-11-07 because JBMC gave no verdict on a regression proof over objects (objects.Kernel#price, lines.Lines#reprice, orders.Orders#reprice within 1800 s, prices.Prices#total within 600 s): finding VF-018. The change under test (lib/src/congruence.rs, used by lib/src/jbmc.rs): a JBMC run without a verdict after 30 s is held still, JBMC writes its formula as SMT-LIB, jvmcontract adds a congruence lemma for every two multiplications of one width (equal operands, in either order, give equal products), and JBMC runs again with Z3 answering that formula; only a proof is taken, otherwise the held run goes on. A probe of lines.Lines#reprice through this path gave Verified in 30.2 s (6 lemmas, 0.2 s of it the attempt), and its defect twin still gave its counterexample from JBMC's own solver in 0.1 s. This job is the finding's closing condition: the tests pass unchanged, including every defect's JVM witness. Some proofs in the prices test are harder for Z3 as well (21 s to more than 30 s with the lemmas), so that test may still meet the 600 s limit on a case other than Prices#total; if it does, the log says which.
expected: cargo exits 0: 9 passed, 0 failed. The three proofs that timed out now end Verified with a checker that reads 'JBMC 6.11.0, its formula decided by Z3 ... multiplication congruence lemma(s)'

resources.notes: the same job took 50m12s on 2026-11-15 with four tests failing at 600 s timeouts (20261115-173209); the three stubborn proofs now take about 30 s each, the prices test is the unknown

steps.name: heap proof tier
steps.run: set -o pipefail; cd lib && JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_MEMORY_MB=2048 cargo test --release --test heap -- --ignored
